summary: This is a batch script (Windows command file) that acts as a command dispatcher for managing a Docker Python container. It checks what action the user wants to perform—like entering bash, building an image, or running a script—and then executes the appropriate Docker commands. If the user doesn't provide a valid action, it shows a help menu explaining all available commands.

explanations.1: @echo off turns off the echoing of commands themselves, so only the output of those commands shows up in the terminal, not the commands that produced it.
explanations.3: cls clears the screen, giving a fresh blank terminal each time you run this script.
explanations.5: This checks if the user provided any argument at all (the %1 variable holds the first argument); if not, jump to the help section to show usage instructions.
explanations.12: This is the hexadecimal encoding of the app name 'app_python', used by Docker's VSCode remote connection feature which expects this format in the URL.
explanations.14: These lines check what the user's first argument was and jump to the matching label (like :bash or :build) to run the correct Docker commands.
explanations.18: When the user wants to start a script, this passes not just the action but also a second argument (%2) which would be the filename like 'main.py'.
explanations.24: This prints the script name itself (%0) as part of the usage message, showing users exactly how to invoke it.
explanations.37: docker compose --env-file loads environment variables from a config file, exec runs a command inside a running container, -it means interactive with a pseudo-terminal, and /bin/bash starts a shell.
explanations.47: This uses a special VSCode URI format to connect to an attached Docker container; the DEV_CODE is the hex-encoded app name that VSCode requires to identify the container.
explanations.56: This checks whether a second argument was provided; if not, show an error message because we need a filename to execute.
explanations.65: The %* variable captures all arguments passed to this label; we store them in a variable so we can manipulate them next.
explanations.66: This removes the first and last character (the double quotes) from the error message using batch string slicing (~1,-1 means 'from position 1 to position -1').
explanations.68: [31m and [0m are ANSI color codes; [31m turns text red and [0m resets to default color, making the error message stand out.
